task: Draft a 50–80-word read-aloud introduction to this fictional lower-elementary mapping activity. The learners know circle, square, and triangle but are new to map keys. Some are using the raised shapes by touch, so explain the key and route without relying on color or pointing. Describe the classroom model, not a real journey. Keep the distinction between a symbol and the thing it represents. No formal references or essay structure are needed.

facts.text: The raised triangle marks the starting place on the classroom map.
A dotted line runs from the triangle to a raised circle, which represents a water bowl.
A raised square represents a bench and is not on the dotted route.
The map's symbols represent places and objects; the raised circle is not itself a bowl containing water.

forbidden_additions: A color-only or pointing-only instruction needed to understand the route
An assertion that the bench lies on the dotted route
An invented real-world destination, distance, or object count
preserve: Triangle means start, circle means water bowl, square means bench
The dotted route ends at the circle
Task-specific explanation of an unfamiliar map key
